title: Turing's model of computation
before: Mathematics could describe calculation procedures, but there was no widely shared formal model of what it means for a problem to be computable by a mechanical process.
problem: Researchers needed a precise way to define algorithms and the limits of mechanical computation.
change: Alan Turing's 1936 work (commonly dated via IEEE Computer Society timeline coverage of the computable-numbers paper) introduced an abstract machine that reads/writes symbols on a tape according to rules—now called the Turing machine.
whyItMattered: It gave computer science a foundation for algorithms, computability, and later programming-language theory.
enabled: Formal reasoning about what computers can and cannot compute; later links to programming and complexity ideas.
modernDescendants: CPU instruction cycles as state machines
concreteExample: Any modern program can be viewed, at a high level, as a finite control logic manipulating memory symbols—an idea rooted in Turing's model.
caveat: Turing machines are a mathematical model, not a claim that Turing built the first electronic computer. Priority debates about early machines are historically complex.
